settings.volcengineSTInfoText: Volcengine Real-time Speech Translation provides text-only translation output. Audio synthesis is not supported in this mode.
settings.volcengineAST2InfoText: Doubao AST 2.0 provides speech-to-speech translation with automatic voice cloning. The translated audio preserves the original speaker's voice characteristics.
settings.volcengineAST2TurnDetectionTooltip:
Auto: server-side voice activity detection. 
Push-to-Talk: hold Space or the mic button to send audio manually. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.volcengineAST2ReplacementLibraryTooltip: Post-transcription regex text substitution. The referenced library must be a regex word list, not a standard replacement list.
settings.volcengineAST2CustomVocabularyFooter: Invalid or empty library IDs are silently ignored — the session runs as if the field weren't set. Library changes made in the Volcengine console can take a few minutes to take effect.
settings.zoomAIInfoText: Zoom Scribe transcribes each utterance and Zoom Translator translates it to text. Translation pairs must include English on one side.
settings.geminiParticipantTokenWarning: Gemini generates audio responses for Other's audio that are discarded, resulting in additional token usage.
settings.helpDiscussionsTooltip: Feature requests, feedback, and community discussions
settings.providerTooltip: Choose your AI translation service. Each service has different features, voices, and pricing. OpenAI offers the most features, while Gemini provides a good free tier. Local (Offline) mode is completely free — no API key or internet required.
settings.modelTooltip: The AI model affects speed and quality. 'Mini' models are faster but simpler. Standard models are more accurate but slightly slower. Try mini first for cost efficiency.
settings.voiceTooltip: Choose the AI's speaking voice. Each voice has different tone and style. Try different ones to find your favorite.
settings.turnDetectionTooltip:
How AI knows when you've finished speaking. 
Normal: Waits for silence. 
Semantic: AI understands context. 
Push-to-Talk: Manual control. 
Push-to-Translate: Manual control with raw mic passthrough to the virtual mic when idle.
settings.thresholdTooltip: Voice detection sensitivity (0.0-1.0). Lower values detect quieter sounds but may trigger accidentally. Higher values need louder speech. Default 0.5 works for most.
settings.prefixPaddingTooltip: Silent time to keep before your speech starts (seconds). Helps capture the beginning of sentences. Too high delays response. Try 0.3-0.5.
settings.silenceDurationTooltip: How long to wait after you stop talking (seconds). Short = quick response but might cut you off. Long = waits patiently but slower. Try 0.5.
settings.silenceDurationTranslateTooltip:
Translate has no server-side turn detection, so these sliders control how the UI splits messages.
Source pause = how long after you stop speaking before a new source-language message starts.
Translation pause = same, but for the translated output (which may run longer than the source because of TTS rendering).
settings.semanticEagernessTooltip:
How quickly AI decides you're done (Semantic mode only). 
Auto: AI decides. 
Low: Very patient. 
Medium: Balanced. 
High: Quick to respond.
settings.temperatureTooltip: Translation creativity (0.0-1.0). Lower = more literal, word-for-word translation. Higher = more natural, conversational style. For translation, 0.7-0.9 works best.
settings.maxTokensTooltip: Maximum length of each translation. Tokens are like word pieces - 100 tokens ≈ 75 words. 2048-4096 good for conversations. 'inf' = unlimited.
settings.transcriptModelTooltip:
Speech recognition model for your own words. This only affects the original text shown next to each translation — the translation itself is produced from your audio directly. 
gpt-live-transcribe: Most accurate, streams as you speak, and the priciest. 
gpt-transcribe: Current generation, transcribes each finished turn. 
gpt-4o-mini-transcribe: Cheapest, the default. 
gpt-4o-transcribe / whisper-1: Older models.
settings.transcriptKeywordsTooltip: Names, jargon, and product terms the transcriber should be ready for, separated by commas. Hints only — a term appears in the transcript only when it is actually spoken. Supported by gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-transcribe.
settings.noiseReductionTooltip:
Background noise removal. 
None: No processing, use in quiet rooms. 
Near field: For headsets/close microphones. 
Far field: For speakers/conference rooms with echo.
settings.systemInstructionsTooltip: Custom instructions for the AI translator. Tell it your preferences like formal/casual tone, technical terms handling, or specific translation style.
settings.transportTypeTooltip:
WebRTC: Lower latency, recommended for most users.
WebSocket: Better compatibility with restrictive networks. Use if WebRTC connection fails.
settings.webrtcVadDisabledTitle: Server VAD is not available in WebRTC mode
settings.webrtcVadNotice: Server VAD is disabled in WebRTC mode. In WebRTC, the server automatically truncates audio when it detects speech, which interrupts translations.
settings.participantInstructionsTooltip:
System instructions for translating Other's audio. If empty, the main instructions above will be used.

Important: Your main instructions may have the wrong language direction for the other side. Example: If you speak Chinese and your main instructions translate Chinese→Japanese, but the other side speaks Japanese, the main instructions would incorrectly try to translate Japanese→Japanese. Set separate Other's instructions to translate Japanese→Chinese.
settings.localTranslationPromptTooltip: Customize how the local translation model is instructed. Only applies to Qwen-family models.
settings.localPromptUnsupported: Current translation model does not support custom prompts. Switch to a Qwen-family model in Model Management to enable.
settings.localPromptNoThinkHint: For Qwen3 models, ` /no_think` will be automatically appended.
settings.participantInstructionsPlaceholder: Leave empty to use main instructions
settings.localInferenceTurnDetectionTooltip:
Auto: local Voice Activity Detection automatically detects speech. 
Push-to-Talk: hold Space or the mic button to send audio manually. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.vadSettingsTooltip: Voice Activity Detection configuration. Adjust these settings to optimize speech detection for your environment.
settings.vadThresholdTooltip: Speech detection sensitivity. Higher values require louder/clearer speech to trigger recognition. Lower values are more sensitive to quiet speech.
settings.vadNegativeThresholdTooltip: Probability below which silence starts counting toward the end of a segment. Auto keeps it 0.15 under the VAD Threshold. It never applies above the VAD Threshold — that would stop segments from ever ending.
settings.vadMinSilenceDurationTooltip: Minimum silence duration to split speech segments. Shorter values split sentences faster, longer values wait for more natural pauses.
settings.vadMinSpeechDurationTooltip: Minimum speech duration to consider as valid speech. Filters out very short sounds like clicks or coughs.
settings.geminiVadTooltip:
Controls how Gemini detects speech pauses to split turns. Adjusting these settings can improve translation responsiveness for continuous speech. 
Push-to-Talk: hold a key to send audio. 
Push-to-Translate: like Push-to-Talk, but routes your raw mic to the virtual mic when idle so you can speak directly without translation.
settings.startOfSpeechSensitivityTooltip: How sensitive the detection is to speech starting. High sensitivity detects quieter or shorter speech onsets.
settings.endOfSpeechSensitivityTooltip: How sensitive the detection is to speech ending. High sensitivity splits turns at shorter pauses, producing more frequent translations.
settings.vadSilenceDurationTooltip: How long a silence must last before it triggers a turn split. Lower values produce faster translations but may split mid-sentence.
settings.vadPrefixPaddingTooltip: Audio padding added before detected speech. Prevents the beginning of words from being cut off.
settings.localInferenceModelsRequired: Please download the required models in <settingsLink>Settings</settingsLink> first. You need to download Speech Recognition (ASR), Translation, and Speech Synthesis (TTS) models to get started.

settings.reasoningEffortTooltip: Controls how much the model deliberates before responding. Higher levels produce better results on complex tasks but increase latency and cost. Recommended: low for live translation. Only available for gpt-realtime-2.
settings.translateInfoBanner: This model stays silent when the speaker uses the same language as the target. Mixed-language speech may have gaps.
settings.translateModelAvailable: API key validated. gpt-realtime-translate is available.

settings.sonioxSharedSessionTooltip:
Both mode can run on one shared Soniox session or a separate session per direction.

Enabled: a single session translates both sides with automatic voice separation — lower cost and latency.

Disabled: a separate session per direction — more reliable when both people talk at once, but about twice the cost.

Only affects Both mode.
settings.sonioxSharedSessionManagedCost: Kizuna AI supports both. Disabled runs two sessions at once — about twice the cost per minute, so your session allowance runs out in about half the time and a higher balance is needed to start.
settings.sonioxAutoParticipantWarning: Set My language to a specific language — with automatic detection, the other side's speech can't be translated into it.
settings.sonioxVocabularyTooltip: Bias recognition toward important names and jargon, and steer how specific terms are translated. Applies from the next session.
settings.sonioxVocabularyTermsTooltip: Improves recognition of uncommon words — names, jargon, product names.
settings.sonioxVocabularyTranslationsTooltip: Biases how specific terms are translated — a preference, not a guaranteed replacement: names with an established rendering work best, while common words may keep the model's own wording. Entries are directional; the reverse direction only exists in Both mode, where you can add a reverse line.
settings.sonioxEndpointSensitivityTooltip: Higher values end utterances sooner — lower latency but more risk of premature cut-offs. Lower values wait longer before finalizing. 0 is the Soniox default.
settings.sonioxEndpointLatencyLevelTooltip: Progressively more aggressive latency reduction when closing an utterance. 0 is the default behavior.
settings.sonioxBackgroundTooltip: Free-form background for the next session — agenda, topic, or reference notes. Helps recognition and translation follow the domain. Trimmed first if the combined context exceeds the size limit.
settings.sonioxBackgroundPlaceholder: Paste an agenda, topic, or background notes (optional)

audioPanel.title: Audio Settings
audioPanel.virtualMicWarningTitle: This is a virtual microphone created by Sokuji.
audioPanel.virtualMicWarningText1: Please do not select this device here. Instead, use this virtual microphone in your video conferencing applications (like Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, etc.) to receive the live speech translation output.
audioPanel.virtualMicWarningText2: For Sokuji to work properly, please select your actual physical microphone from the list.
audioPanel.loopbackMicWarningTitle: This input re-captures what this computer is playing.
audioPanel.loopbackMicWarningText1: Loopback inputs like "Stereo Mix" or a "Monitor of ..." device record the system's own audio output. During a session that includes Sokuji's translated speech, Sokuji would hear and translate itself in a loop.
audioPanel.loopbackMicWarningText2: The device stays selected in case this routing is intentional, but for normal use please pick a physical microphone instead.
audioPanel.virtualSpeakerWarningTitle: This is a virtual speaker created by Sokuji.
audioPanel.virtualSpeakerWarningText1: Please do not select this device as your monitor. The Sokuji_Virtual_Speaker is used by Sokuji to output audio to your conferencing applications.
audioPanel.virtualSpeakerWarningText2: Connecting your monitor to Sokuji's output device would create an audio feedback loop, causing your input to contain your own monitored output.
audioPanel.virtualSpeakerWarningText3: The "Turn On" switch connects the virtual speaker to your selected monitor device, allowing you to hear what's being sent to your conferencing application. The "Turn Off" switch disconnects this monitoring connection.
audioPanel.virtualSpeakerWarningText4: For proper operation, please select a different monitor device (like your headphones or speakers) from the list.
audioPanel.realVoicePassthroughDescription: Pass your original audio (speaker's voice) directly to the virtual microphone so listeners can hear both original and translated audio
audioPanel.passthroughManagedByPushToTranslate: In Push-to-Translate mode, passthrough is automatic — it plays at 100% volume when you're not holding the key, and stops (audio goes to translation) while you hold it.
audioPanel.mutualExclusivitySpeakerText: Please turn off Other's audio before enabling the speaker monitor.
audioPanel.mutualExclusivityParticipantText: Please turn off the speaker monitor before enabling Other's audio.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText1: Other's audio requires Screen Recording permission to capture system audio.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText2: Please go to System Preferences > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and enable Sokuji.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText3: After enabling the permission, please restart the app.
audioPanel.monitorLockedByMode: Speaker monitoring is only available in "{{mode}}" mode — it cannot run alongside Other's audio without causing echo. Switch the translation mode to "{{mode}}" to re-enable it.
audioPanel.participantSourceDesc: Choose which application to translate. System Audio captures everything you hear, including games and music.
audioPanel.participantSilentNoPermission: The selected application is sending no audio. If you are on macOS, allow Sokuji under System Settings > Privacy & Security > System Audio Recording Only, then restart the session.
audioPanel.audioCaptureDeniedText1: Capturing one application needs the "System Audio Recording Only" permission. Without it macOS delivers silence instead of an error, so the session runs but nothing is translated.
audioPanel.audioCaptureDeniedText2: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > System Audio Recording Only and enable Sokuji.
audioPanel.audioCaptureDeniedText3: Sokuji only appears in that list after it has tried to capture once, which it just did. Restart the session after enabling it.
audioPanel.screenRecordingDeniedText2Named: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and enable "{{app}}".
audioPanel.audioCaptureDeniedText2Named: Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > System Audio Recording Only and enable "{{app}}".
audioPanel.audioCaptureDeniedText3Named: "{{app}}" only appears in that list after it has tried to capture once, which it just did. Restart the session after enabling it.
audioPanel.screenRecordingHasAlternative: You can avoid this permission entirely: pick a specific application as Other's audio source instead. Applications only appear in that list while they are playing audio.
audioPanel.participantSourceSwitchFailed: Could not switch Other's audio source. Stop and start the session to change it.
audioPanel.participantFellBackToSystemAudio: Capture of the selected application stopped, so all system audio is being translated instead. Pick the application again to narrow it back.

welcome.title: Welcome to Sokuji
welcome.content: Welcome to Sokuji! This simple guide will help you start using real-time translation in just a few steps.

mode.content: Choose what Sokuji translates: Me — your own voice (so the other side understands you); Other — what the other side says (so you understand them); or Both for two-way translation. This decides which audio is captured — pick Other or Both to turn on Other's audio.
mode.title: Translation mode

settings.title: Step 1: Open Settings
settings.content: Click here to open Settings where you can configure your languages and audio devices.

languages.title: Step 2: Choose Languages
languages.content: Select My language (what you speak) and Other's language (what you want the other side to hear).

microphone.title: Step 4: Select Microphone
microphone.content: Select your microphone from the list. This is what will capture your voice.

speaker.title: Step 5: Select Speaker
speaker.content: Choose a monitoring device to preview the translation. Translated audio is always output to the virtual microphone regardless of monitoring. Select Sokuji Virtual Microphone as the microphone input in your meeting app or website. Headphones are recommended for monitoring to avoid feedback.

systemAudio.title: Step 6: Other's Audio
systemAudio.content: This is the Other channel — what other people say, translated for you. Turn it on by choosing Other or Both in the translation mode (it stays off in Me mode). In the browser extension, it captures the current tab so you can translate the other side in Google Meet, Teams, or Zoom. In the desktop app, it captures all system audio, so you can translate YouTube, Twitch, Netflix, or any source. The other side's speech is translated to text only — no speech synthesis. Together with your microphone, this gives full two-way translation.

start.title: Step 7: Start Translating
start.content: Click 'Start' to begin translating! Just speak naturally and hear the translation in real-time.

complete.title: All Set!
complete.content: Perfect! You're ready to use Sokuji. Click Start and begin speaking to hear real-time translations.

provider.title: Step 3: Translation Provider
provider.content: Choose your translation provider. Sokuji has its own built-in service — sign in from the account button in the title bar to use it. It also supports cloud services like OpenAI, Gemini, Volcengine (Doubao), and more, where you bring your own API key. You can also use Local Inference — no API key needed, free and privacy-focused, just download models for fully offline translation.

welcome.title: Welcome to Sokuji
welcome.content: Welcome to Sokuji! This guide will help you set up the extension for live speech translation. Let's get started!

mode.content: Choose what Sokuji translates: Me — your own voice (so the other side understands you); Other — what the other side says (so you understand them); or Both for two-way translation. This decides which audio is captured — pick Other or Both to turn on Other's audio.
mode.title: Translation mode

settings.title: Step 1: Open Settings
settings.content: First, let's configure your settings. Click here to open the Settings panel where you can choose your translation provider and customize settings.

apiKey.title: Step 2: Translation Provider
apiKey.content: Choose your translation provider. Sokuji supports cloud services like OpenAI, Gemini, Volcengine (Doubao), and more. You can also use Local Inference — no API key needed, free and privacy-focused, just download models for fully offline translation.

systemInstructions.title: Step 3: System Instructions
systemInstructions.content: Customize the system instructions to control how the AI responds. You can modify the translation behavior and add specific requirements here.

voiceSettings.title: Step 4: Voice Settings
voiceSettings.content: Configure the voice type that will be used for speech synthesis. Choose from different voice options to match your preference.

turnDetection.title: Step 5: Turn Detection
turnDetection.content: Configure automatic turn detection settings including detection mode, threshold, and audio parameters for optimal speech recognition performance.

microphoneSetup.title: Step 6: Microphone Setup
microphoneSetup.content: Select your microphone device here. Make sure to choose the correct input device for the best audio quality.

speakerSetup.title: Step 7: Speaker Setup
speakerSetup.content: Select a monitoring device to listen to the translated audio and verify if it meets your requirements. It is recommended to use headphones for monitoring to avoid interference with microphone input. When you are satisfied with the translation settings, it is suggested to turn off monitoring so you can focus more on your expression without microphone interference.

systemAudio.title: Step 8: Other's Audio
systemAudio.content: This is the Other channel — what other people say, translated for you. Turn it on by choosing Other or Both in the translation mode (it stays off in Me mode). In the browser extension, it captures the current tab so you can translate the other side in Google Meet, Teams, or Zoom. In the desktop app, it captures all system audio, so you can translate YouTube, Twitch, Netflix, or any source. The other side's speech is translated to text only — no speech synthesis. Together with your microphone, this gives full two-way translation.

startSession.title: Step 9: Start Session
startSession.content: Click the "Start Session" button to begin using Sokuji. Once started, you can speak naturally for live translation. If Automatic turn detection is disabled, use "Push to Talk" (Space key) to speak.

complete.title: Setup Guide Complete!
complete.content: Great! You're all set up. Remember to grant microphone permissions when prompted. You can restart this guide anytime from the settings.
